title: Script the quality-gates JSON artifact write
description:
The artifact write landed as prose in `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md` Step 5 (bead tadw-qg-json-verdict-artifact-21l). The model reassembles the schema on every run, and the pre-push consumer treats an unparseable or field-shifted artifact the same as no artifact: it warns and allows. So a drifted write disables the verdict gate without ever saying so, which is the exact silent-degradation failure mode the doc-freshness and secrets gates were scripted to avoid.

Design: a stdlib-only `skills/quality-gates/scripts/write_report_json.py` mirroring `check_doc_paths.py` and `check_secrets.py` conventions. It takes the gate rows and the verdict on stdin as JSON, derives head, dirty, and timestamp from git itself rather than trusting the caller to retype them, validates `verdict` against the four Verdict Rules strings, and exits 2 when the tree is not a git repository. Then point Step 5 at the script instead of at the inline python3.

Not folded into tadw-qg-json-verdict-artifact-21l on purpose: that bead's own estimate is 3 files and 80 LOC of prose, and a script plus its pinned suite is a separate unit of roughly 300 LOC.

title: Fix the command/skill namespace collision in all 18 commands that delegate with 'load the skill'
description:
A command file and a skill directory that share a name also share one `tadw:` invocation namespace, and the command wins. When such a command's body says "Use the `<name>` skill", invoking it returns the command body, whose first line redirects to itself, so the skill is never loaded.

This is not theoretical. `/bead-audit-all` shipped this way and every backlog sweep it ran scored from a twenty-line summary instead of the 661-line rubric, reporting confident numbers computed from nothing. A wrong number produced this way is indistinguishable downstream from a right one, which is what makes the class dangerous rather than merely untidy.

18 commands collide by name, and the triage below shows all 18 delegate. `/bead-audit-all` is not one of them: no `skills/bead-audit-all/` exists, so it never collided. Its 2.4.1 fix is the pattern to copy, not a reduction of the work.

## Triage result (completed 2026-08-09)

All 18 colliding commands delegate by name. **Zero are self-contained.** An earlier read of this bead assumed body length was a proxy for safety; it is not. Commands with 10 to 20 lines of their own instructions still open with "Use the `<name>` skill", so they redirect exactly like the one-line ones.

Total skill content unreachable by name: **271,067 bytes.**

| Command | Skill bytes shadowed |
|---|---|
| /bead-audit | 51,113 |
| /plan-to-beads | 31,438 |
| /ux-audit-ios | 22,598 |
| /product-surface-docs | 18,979 |
| /ux-audit | 18,291 |
| /plan-review | 16,858 |
| /ab-test-design | 13,614 |
| /product-roadmap | 12,830 |
| /product-research | 12,492 |
| /research-ingest | 12,193 |
| /agentic-clean-code | 11,288 |
| /competitive-analysis | 10,702 |
| /product-brief | 9,257 |
| /aso-audit | 8,933 |
| /verify-acceptance | 8,314 |
| /roadmap-dashboard | 7,596 |
| /business-ideas | 2,740 |
| /idea-wizard | 1,831 |

Classification test used: the command body matches `(use|load|invoke) the \`?<name>\`? skill` and contains no `SKILL.md` read. Reproduce it by re-running that match over `commands/` against the `skills/` directory names.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `/bead-audit` on any bead, in a session with the plugin loaded.
2. Watch which file the Skill tool returns. It is `commands/bead-audit.md` (20 lines), not `skills/bead-audit/SKILL.md` (661 lines).
3. Confirm the substitution directly: the returned body carries the resolved `$ARGUMENTS` value, which only a command receives.

Expected: the audit rubric loads. Actual: the command body loads and redirects to itself.

The 18 colliding names, from `comm -12` over `commands/` and `skills/`: ab-test-design, agentic-clean-code, aso-audit, bead-audit, business-ideas, competitive-analysis, idea-wizard, plan-review, plan-to-beads, product-brief, product-research, product-roadmap, product-surface-docs, research-ingest, roadmap-dashboard, ux-audit, ux-audit-ios, verify-acceptance.

## Why the runtime does this

`claude plugin details tadw` reports 72 registered skills for 35 skill directories and 37 commands. Commands and skills occupy one namespace, and each colliding name holds two entries. The cost table shows both, for example `plan-review ~50 always-on ~6.2k on-invoke` (the skill) beside `plan-review ~50 always-on ~330 on-invoke` (the command). The command's description is the one surfaced to the model.
design:
Three fixes exist, and the choice is per command. The triage is done, so every one of the 18 needs one of them.

**A. Read the skill from disk.** Replace the delegating line with an explicit `Read` of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, plus a `Glob` fallback and an assertion that named headings are present in the file that was read. This is what `/response-style` and `/bead-audit-all` do. Keeps the command name. Costs a hardcoded path per command, forever, and the pattern must be remembered for every command written afterward.

**C. Delete the command and let the skill take the name.** Verified empirically on 2026-08-09: `commands/competitive-analysis.md` was moved out of the installed plugin, the registered skill count fell from 72 to 71, the surviving entry kept the skill's on-invoke cost (~3.9k, not the command's ~0.1k), and after a restart the slash menu showed the skill's own description ("Deep competitor teardown with positioning map, moat analysis, feature gaps..."). The file was restored and the plugin re-validated at exit 0.

Nothing is lost that matters. `$ARGUMENTS` still works, since four skills already use it. Only `argument-hint` is lost, which is a menu display hint rather than behavior. Deleting also repairs the agents: `agents/product-manager.md` tells itself to load these same skills by name and hits the identical dead end today.

**B. Rename one side.** Give the command a distinct name so no collision exists. This is what 19 of the 37 commands already do (`/fresh-eyes-cr` for `review-fresh-eyes`, `/prod-ops` for `production-ops`). Breaks any hardcoded invocation path in other repos.

**Recommended: C for any command whose content is skill content, A for any command that carries genuine per-invocation instructions worth keeping under a slash name.** C is preferred by default because it removes the collision rather than working around it, and costs nothing afterward.

The governing rule to encode: **a command may share a skill's name, or delegate to that skill by name, but never both.**

Sequence. Fix `/bead-audit` first, since 2.4.1 ships a README callout telling users to avoid it. For each remaining command, decide C or A by asking whether the body says anything that is not already the skill's job; most of it (for example `/ux-audit` naming the `ux-product-designer` role) reads like skill content and should move into the skill before the command is deleted.

Guard against regression with a check in `hooks/test-hooks.js`, which already asserts that `/response-style` reads its skill file rather than invoking it. Generalize that check to every colliding name.
acceptance_criteria:
1. MET. Every one of the 18 colliding names is resolved: 8 by deletion (7 in 2.5.0 plus /bead-audit in 2.4.2), 10 by reading the SKILL.md from disk. Re-running the triage match over commands/ returns zero.
2. MET. Nothing needed moving. Each deleted command's body was a precis of its skill; /business-ideas and /idea-wizard duplicated a step already at line 12 of their own SKILL.md. The commits name this per command.
3. MET, 2026-08-09, after installing 2.5.0 and restarting. The menu shows the skill's own description for bead-audit ("against the Marr audit, size audit, type-specific section audit, and a grounding audit against the current main branch") rather than the deleted command's ("against the Marr, size, and type-specific section standards"). Verified by resolution rather than by grepping the loaded body; the description comes from the skill's frontmatter, so the file being read is the skill.
4. MET. Check 18 in hooks/test-hooks.js. Proven to discriminate, not merely to pass: injecting a delegate-by-name regression into /ux-audit exits 1 naming that command; removing only its Glob fallback exits 1 naming that; restoring leaves the file byte-identical and the suite green.
5. AMENDED, then MET. Originally: "a registered skill count equal to (skill directories + surviving commands), with no name appearing twice." The count holds: 64 = 35 + 29. The second clause does not, and it was wrong when written. It assumed every collision would be eliminated; the chosen design keeps 10 commands that share a name and read from disk, so those 10 names register twice on purpose. Amended clause: no name may appear twice unless its command reads the skill from disk, which check 18 enforces.
6. MET. The /bead-audit callout in README.md now says the command file was removed and the skill takes the slash name. AGENTS.md carries the namespace rule instead of the "only /bead-audit-all has been fixed" wording.
7. MET. rumdl fmt --check . clean over 106 files; 19 hook checks pass with the docs/HOOKS.md count verified; claude plugin validate . exits 0; 25 framework-leak checks pass.
8. MET. business-ideas and idea-wizard are referenced by no agent and no command. Accepted and recorded in AGENTS.md: both are invoked directly as /<name>, so a referrer would add nothing. No other skill was orphaned; 33 of 35 remain referenced.
notes:
Done when every command that collides with a same-named skill either loads that skill's real content or does not claim to, and a test fails if a new delegating collision is introduced.

Triage is complete as of 2026-08-09: all 18 delegate, none are self-contained, so the size is no longer provisional. The earlier 'Stretch (provisional)' band assumed only a subset would need work.

Not done when the 18 are merely surveyed. The survey is finished; the edits are the deliverable.

Option C (delete the command, let the skill take the name) was verified empirically on 2026-08-09 by moving commands/competitive-analysis.md out of the installed plugin and restarting. Details in the Design field.

title: Remove the 104 remaining em-dashes across 10 agent, command, and skill files
description:
The house style rule forbids em-dashes and en-dashes everywhere: prose, code, comments, commit messages, docs, and UI copy. 104 occurrences remain across 10 files in `agents/`, `commands/`, and `skills/`. Release 2.4.1 cleaned only the nine in `README.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

One subset is worse than the rest. Some of these sit inside **output templates that an agent fills in and emits**, not in prose describing the agent. `agents/product-analyst.md:78` is `- **Feature Name** <em-dash> Description`, inside that agent's Output Format block alongside `[2-3 paragraphs providing...]` placeholders. Every product analysis that agent writes therefore carries em-dashes into a delivered document. That is the rule being broken at runtime, in work handed to a reader, rather than in a file only a maintainer opens.

Counts by file: `agents/product-analyst.md` 31, `skills/agentic-clean-code/SKILL.md` 19, `agents/diagnostician.md` 14, `skills/business-ideas/SKILL.md` 14, `skills/architecture-decision-record/SKILL.md` 11, `skills/idea-wizard/SKILL.md` 9, `commands/diagnose.md` 2, `commands/product-analysis.md` 2, `commands/quality-gates.md` 1, `skills/production-ops/SKILL.md` 1.
design:
Do the template files first, in their own commit, because they leak into generated output: `agents/product-analyst.md`, `agents/diagnostician.md`, and `skills/architecture-decision-record/SKILL.md`. The prose remainder can follow in a second commit.

Do **not** run a blanket `sed`. The replacement is context-dependent and a global substitution produces wrong punctuation:

- Term followed by a definition in a list: use ` - `, matching the convention the registered-component lists in `AGENTS.md` already use.
- A parenthetical clause inside a sentence: use a comma pair, or parentheses.
- A heading label such as `### Pipeline A <em-dash> Business Planning`: use a colon.

Read each line and choose. 104 lines is small enough that judgment beats automation here.

Prevent regression with a check. `hooks/test-hooks.js` is the existing home for repo-wide assertions and runs on Node built-ins only, so add the scan there rather than introducing new tooling. The check must exempt nothing silently: if a file genuinely needs a dash character, it should fail and force an explicit decision.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A scan for U+2014 (em dash) and U+2013 (en dash) over `agents/`, `commands/`, `skills/`, `README.md`, and `AGENTS.md` returns zero matches. Use the scan added in criterion 4 as the authority, so the bead and the check agree on one definition of "clean".
2. Replacements are context-appropriate, not mechanical: spot-checking ten changed lines shows list definitions using " - ", parentheticals using commas or parentheses, and heading labels using a colon.
3. The template subset (`agents/product-analyst.md`, `agents/diagnostician.md`, `skills/architecture-decision-record/SKILL.md`) lands in its own commit, ahead of the prose remainder.
4. A check in `hooks/test-hooks.js` fails when any tracked markdown file outside the documented exemptions contains U+2014 or U+2013. Verified to discriminate by adding one and observing a non-zero exit.
5. The exemption list, if any, is written in the check itself with a reason per entry, not implied by a path glob.
6. `node hooks/test-hooks.js` passes and its stated check count matches the number it runs.
7. No prose was reworded beyond the punctuation change. Verified by reading the diff: every hunk changes punctuation only.
notes:
Done when no em-dash or en-dash remains in any file this repo owns, and a new one cannot be added without a test failing.

Deliberately out of scope: `CHANGELOG.md` history below the current release, since rewriting shipped release notes changes the record of what was said at the time.

## Estimated size

11 files (the 10 carrying dashes, plus `hooks/test-hooks.js` for the regression check), ~134 LOC, band: Too big by file count (provisional - inferred from the How, author to confirm).

The LOC is well inside Target; only the file count pushes it over. The How already sequences this as two commits, template subset first and prose remainder second, so splitting the bead along that same seam gives two Target-band beads: the template subset is 3 files plus the check, and the remainder is 7 files. Split before claiming.

title: Strip ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in evals/run.py so a set key cannot fail every case
description:
## Why (Computational)

evals/run.py shells out to `claude -p`. When ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in the environment, that
call exits 1 with a warning that claude.ai connectors are disabled because an API key takes
precedence over the claude.ai login. Every case then fails at the 'invocation' check.

Measured 2026-08-05: a full six-case run scored 0 of 6 for this reason alone. Re-running the
same tree with `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` scored 3 of 6. Nothing about the failure output says
'your environment is wrong'; it reads like six style failures, and the summary line reports a
score as though the suite had measured something.

The stakeholder is anyone who runs the suite from a shell that exports the key, which includes
any agent session started with one. A suite that reports a confident wrong number is worse than
one that refuses to run.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Export `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the shell.
2. Run `python3 evals/run.py`.
3. Run the same tree again as `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY python3 evals/run.py` and compare the
   two summary lines.

**Expected behavior:** the suite either invokes the model and grades each case, or refuses to
run and says the environment is at fault.

**Actual behavior:** step 2 fails all six cases at the `invocation` check and prints 0 of 6 as
though it had measured style. Step 3 scores 3 of 6 on the identical tree. Nothing in the step-2
output attributes the failure to the environment.

**Environment / version:** main. `ask` is at `evals/run.py:69` and its `subprocess.run` call at
`evals/run.py:74` passes no `env=` argument, so the child inherits the exported key.
design:
In ask(), build the child environment explicitly instead of inheriting the parent's:

    child_env = os.environ.copy()
    removed = [k for k in ('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY',) if child_env.pop(k, None)]

and pass env=child_env to subprocess.run. Print one line per run when a variable was removed, so
the behavior is visible rather than magic.

Keep the removal list explicit and short. Do not strip anything else on speculation; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
is the variable measured to break the call.

Alternative rejected: documenting the workaround in evals/README.md and leaving the code alone.
That is what exists today, and it leaves the trap armed for anyone who does not read the README
first, which is everyone running the suite from an agent session.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in the environment, when `python3 evals/run.py --case exact-names --runs 1` runs, then the case invokes the model and produces real grader output rather than an invocation failure.
2. Given the same run, when the output is read, then it states once that ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was removed from the child environment.
3. Given ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set, when the suite runs, then behavior and output are unchanged from today, with no note printed.
4. Given the fix has landed, when evals/README.md is read, then the 'Running it' workaround note is replaced by a statement of what the runner does.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- The suite runs correctly with the key set, and says once that it removed it.
- The suite is byte-identical in behavior when the key is absent.
- The README workaround note is gone, replaced by a description of the behavior.

## Estimated size
2 files (`evals/run.py`, `evals/README.md`), ~10 LOC. Band: Trivial.

Trivial carries a standing warn that work this small is usually a direct commit rather than a
bead. It is kept as a bead deliberately: the change is what makes the eval suite's scores
trustworthy, and a suite that silently reported 0 of 6 needs its correction on the record
rather than buried in a drive-by commit.

title: Evaluate style-testing efficacy with a fixture-based blind A/B harness
description:
## Why (Computational)

Part 1 (tadw-wdk) can prove style-testing is correct-by-construction, wired, and reachable. It
cannot prove it is useful. The central risk Part 1 names is that the core "reduces to platitudes
once the framework nouns are removed", and Part 1 ships no detector for that: its gates check
token hygiene and invocation, not whether the skill changes the tests a model actually writes.

A prompt document with no behavioral evaluation is an unverified claim. The stakeholder is the
owner, who will otherwise adopt this skill across every language they work in on the strength of
its prose alone, and any future editor, who needs a regression signal before changing its wording.

Plan: docs/plans/feature-plan-style-testing-part-2.md (M5b)

## Estimated size
9 files (4 fixture sources, 4 rubrics, 1 protocol), about 340 LOC, plus 36 model runs for tier 2
and 4 probes for tier 3. Band: Stretch.

Stretch is justified because the nine files are four near-identical fixture-and-rubric pairs
plus one protocol document, so the novel design surface is one fixture shape and one protocol,
not nine independent units. The model runs are effort rather than diff and do not enter the band.
design:
Four fixtures, one per framework the appendix covers: pytest, Vitest, XCTest, Minitest. Each
source file is 40 to 80 lines containing a happy path, an error path, a boundary condition, and at
least two nondeterminism traps (an injectable clock, an unordered collection, a record best
located by unique key). Each rubric.md holds 10 binary criteria derived from the 14 principles.

D8, trap subset. Three of the 10 criteria are pre-registered, before any run, as the ones an
unguided model reliably fails. They carry the discriminating weight. This exists because current
models write decent tests unprompted: if baseline already scores 8 or 9 of 10, a "strictly greater
in aggregate" bar is unachievable through no fault of the skill, and invites exactly the
bar-lowering the plan warns against.

D9, blind per-criterion judging. A third subagent sees both suites labeled A and B in randomized
order and scores each criterion independently with cited evidence. The treatment suite is often
self-identifying through its scenario naming and hoisted setup, so the blinding limitation is
stated in eval-protocol.md rather than claimed away. Per-criterion scoring with evidence is robust
to a judge who guesses the arm; a holistic preference score is not.

D10, smoke check first. One arm-pair per fixture (12 runs) gates the full 36-run matrix. A fixture
whose baseline passes all three traps is a broken fixture, not a null result, and is redesigned
before the full matrix runs.

Pass bar, all four must hold: treatment median at least 8 of 10 on every fixture; treatment at
least equal to baseline on every fixture; treatment strictly greater than baseline on the trap
subset on every fixture; zero framework-inappropriate advice.

Tier 3 after tier 2 clears: unseen-framework probe (Go testing, deliberately absent from the
appendix), RSpec non-regression diffed against the pre-rewrite SHA captured in Part 1's M2,
escape-hatch probe, and live dogfood writing real tests in a real project and running them.

A failing fixture produces a finding and a follow-up bead against the skill's wording. The bar is
never adjusted to fit the result.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the four fixtures each carry a rubric.md with 10 binary criteria, when inspected before any eval run, then exactly 3 criteria per fixture are marked as the pre-registered trap subset.
2. Given the smoke check (one arm-pair per fixture, 12 runs), when run, then no fixture's baseline passes all 3 trap criteria; any fixture that does is redesigned before the full matrix.
3. Given the full tier-2 matrix, when scored, then treatment median is at least 8 of 10 on every fixture, at least equal to baseline on every fixture, and strictly greater than baseline on the trap subset on every fixture.
4. Given the tier-2 results, when reviewed, then zero treatment outputs contain advice inappropriate to that fixture's framework.
5. Given the tier-3 unseen-framework probe against Go's testing package, when a model applies style-testing, then the output applies the core principles and invents no idiom from a different language.
6. Given the tier-3 RSpec non-regression probe diffed against the pre-rewrite SHA from Part 1's M2, when compared, then the post-rewrite output is at least as good as the pre-rewrite output.
7. Given the tier-3 dogfood, when the generated tests are run in a real project, then they pass.
8. Given eval-protocol.md, when read, then it states the blinding limitation explicitly rather than claiming the judge cannot infer the arm.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- skills/style-testing/references/fixtures/ holds 4 fixture directories, each with a source file and a 10-criterion rubric marking 3 traps.
- skills/style-testing/references/eval-protocol.md documents the arms, the blind judging procedure, the stated blinding limitation, and the pass bar.
- The 12-run smoke check passes and confirms every fixture's traps discriminate.
- The full tier-2 matrix clears all four pass-bar conditions.
- All four tier-3 probes pass, including live dogfood tests that actually run green.

## Scope boundary
Changing the skill's content in response to eval results is OUT of scope. A failing fixture
produces a finding and a follow-up bead, so the eval stays an honest measurement rather than
something the skill is tuned against.

title: Cover the drifted and satisfied grounding band ceilings with a pinned fixture repository
description:
The Grounding Audit added in 2.4.1 applies two band ceilings: `drifted` caps a bead at Adequate, `satisfied` caps it at Weak. Neither ceiling has ever fired in a test.

The eight existing fixtures under `skills/bead-audit/references/fixtures/` are pasted bodies that name no repository of record, so all eight are `ungroundable`, which applies no ceiling. They prove the ceilings do **not** fire when they should not, and prove nothing about whether they fire when they should. The only check on that arithmetic today is a worked-example table in `SKILL.md`, which is prose an author wrote, not a computation anyone ran.

This matters more than a typical coverage gap because a ceiling that silently stops working produces a *higher* score, not a lower one. A regression here reports a stale bead as Excellent, which is exactly the failure the Grounding Audit was built to prevent.
design:
The obstacle is that grounding needs a real repository at a known sha, and the current suite is pasted text with no repo behind it.

**Option A: a committed fixture repository.** Add `skills/bead-audit/references/fixtures/repo/` as a small tree of real files, plus fixture beads that name it as their repository of record. Self-contained and offline, but a nested git repository inside this one is awkward to commit and easy to break.

**Option B (preferred): ground against this repository at a pinned sha.** Write fixture beads whose claims reference real paths in `tadw` at a specific commit, chosen so the outcome is fixed forever. A `drifted` fixture claims a file that was renamed between two known commits; a `satisfied` fixture states an end condition that a known commit already satisfies. Store the sha in the fixture body, and have the check pass it explicitly rather than resolving `origin/main`, so history moving does not change the answer.

Option B needs no nested repository and exercises the real `git show` and `git grep` path. Its risk is that a fixture reads as a repo-history trivia question, so each one must state in a comment which commit it pins and why that commit makes the outcome permanent.

Add at minimum: one `drifted` fixture whose expected band would be Excellent but is capped to Adequate, and one `satisfied` fixture capped to Weak. Extend `references/fixtures/README.md`, which currently documents these two states as deliberately uncovered.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A fixture exists whose grounding verdict is `drifted`, whose raw score would band Excellent, and whose expected band is Adequate.
2. A fixture exists whose grounding verdict is `satisfied` and whose expected band is Weak.
3. Both fixtures pin an explicit sha in their body, and re-running them after new commits land on main produces the same verdict. Verified by running them twice with a commit in between.
4. Each fixture states, in the fixture itself, which commit it pins and why that commit fixes the outcome permanently.
5. Discrimination is verified, not assumed: deleting the `drifted` ceiling row from the rubric makes fixture 1 report Excellent and fail; deleting the `satisfied` row makes fixture 2 fail.
6. The eight existing fixtures still report their documented bands, confirming the new fixtures did not change how the ungroundable path behaves.
7. `skills/bead-audit/references/fixtures/README.md` no longer says the two ceilings are uncovered, and the matching sentence in `AGENTS.md` and the Known issues entry in `CHANGELOG.md` are updated.
notes:
Done when removing either ceiling from the rubric makes a fixture fail.

Not done when a fixture merely exists and reports the right band. The test is discrimination: an untested guard and a guard that cannot fail are the same thing.

## Estimated size

~4 files (2 new fixture bodies, `skills/bead-audit/references/fixtures/README.md`, and the matching sentences in `AGENTS.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`), ~150 LOC, band: Target (provisional - inferred from the How, author to confirm).

title: Fix false plugin.json component-registration claims in AGENTS.md
description:
## Why (Computational)

AGENTS.md makes three false claims about .claude-plugin/plugin.json:

- Line 355: plugin.json "defines plugin metadata, component registration, and the hooks field"
- Line 529 (Adding a New Skill): "Register in .claude-plugin/plugin.json if needed"
- Line 537 (Adding a New Agent): "Register in .claude-plugin/plugin.json if needed"

plugin.json is 511 bytes containing name, version, description, author, license, and hooks. It
registers zero components. `grep -c "style-python\|style-frontend\|review-python"
.claude-plugin/plugin.json` returns 0. Skills, agents, and commands are auto-discovered from their
directories; the real registration surfaces are the AGENTS.md component lists and the README table.

This is not cosmetic. The defect already produced an unsatisfiable acceptance criterion in this
tracker: bead tadw-wdk's original AC #3 required `grep -rw style-testing
.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to match, which can never pass. Every agent or human who follows
AGENTS.md to add a component will keep generating the same bad work item until the instruction is
corrected. The stakeholder is anyone extending this plugin, including future agent sessions.

Plan: docs/plans/feature-plan-style-testing-part-2.md (M4)

## Estimated size
1 file, about 6 lines changed. Band: below Target. Justified as a standalone bead because it is
independent of all style-testing work and blocks nothing.
design:
Fix the instruction, not just the description (D11). Correcting line 355 alone would leave 529 and
537 still telling readers to edit plugin.json, and those two lines are what actually caused the
defect.

- Line 355: state that skills, agents, and commands are auto-discovered from their directories,
  and that plugin.json carries metadata plus the hooks field only.
- Lines 529 and 537: replace "Register in .claude-plugin/plugin.json if needed" with the true
  surfaces, namely the AGENTS.md component lists and the README.md table.

Sequence after Part 1 (tadw-wdk). Part 1's M3 also edits AGENTS.md, at lines 168 and 362. The
concerns are disjoint (component lists versus plugin.json claims) but running both concurrently
against the same file invites a needless conflict.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given `grep -n "plugin.json" AGENTS.md`, when run, then no matching line instructs registering a skill, agent, or command in plugin.json.
2. Given a reader follows the AGENTS.md "Adding a New Skill" steps end to end, when they finish, then they have edited no file under .claude-plugin/.
3. Given AGENTS.md line 355, when read, then it states that components are auto-discovered from their directories and no longer claims plugin.json performs component registration.
4. Given AGENTS.md lines 529 and 537, when read, then each names the AGENTS.md component list and the README table as the registration surfaces.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- No line in AGENTS.md instructs registering a component in .claude-plugin/plugin.json.
- Line 355 describes auto-discovery and scopes plugin.json to metadata plus the hooks field.
- The "Adding a New Skill" and "Adding a New Agent" steps name the true registration surfaces.

## Note
plugin.json itself is NOT changed. The auto-discovery behavior is correct; the documentation
describing it is what is wrong.
close_reason: Fixed in 1.18.1: AGENTS.md no longer claims plugin.json performs component registration, and the Adding a New Skill/Agent steps name the real surfaces

title: Cover the untested-change and planted-secret findings with fixture evals
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 2 and Gate 6 are the two gates most likely to be quietly weakened, since one is
judgment and the other is a pattern list. Nothing currently checks that the skill reports a
finding when a real defect is present, only that it reports nothing when the tree is clean.

The stakeholder is anyone who trusts a clean report on a repository that has an untested branch
or a committed key.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M6)

## Estimated size

5 files, about 130 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Two fixture repositories and two single-arm cases.

`gates-untested-change` plants a new function with a branch and no test anywhere. It asserts the
change-coverage gate reports FAIL with the case enumerated, not merely that something failed.

`gates-planted-secret` plants a fake `AKIA` key in a source file. It asserts the secrets gate
reports FAIL with a `file:line`, and, critically, that the key's value appears nowhere in the
report.

That last assertion mirrors at the report level the rule `test_check_secrets.py` pins at the
script level. Checking it in both places means a leak is caught wherever it is introduced,
whether in the script's output or in the skill's prose about how to render a finding.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the `gates-untested-change` fixture, when the case runs, then the report grades change coverage FAIL and enumerates the untested case.
2. Given the `gates-planted-secret` fixture, when the case runs, then the report shows a secrets FAIL with a `file:line`.
3. Given the same run, when scanning the whole report text, then the planted key's value does not appear.
4. Given three runs of each case, when the suite finishes, then all three pass for each.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `gates-untested-change` and `gates-planted-secret` exist with their fixtures
- Each passes three runs out of three
- The planted-secret case asserts the key's value is absent from the report

title: Teach the eval harness to run in a fixture repository
description:
## Why (Computational)

`evals/run.py` hardcodes `cwd=REPO_ROOT` inside `ask()`, so every case runs against
this repository and no case can plant a defect. That single line is why the skill's behavior has
never been tested.

The stakeholder is any future editor of `skills/quality-gates/SKILL.md`, who today has no
regression signal at all: every rule not converted into a script is unprotected prose.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M6)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 160 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Two optional `case.json` keys, both backward compatible with the six existing
cases.

A `fixture` key names a directory under `evals/fixtures/`. The harness copies it to a temp
directory, initializes it as a git repository with one commit, applies the case's planted defect,
and passes that directory as `cwd` instead of `REPO_ROOT`.

A `single_arm` key runs only the with-plugin arm. A slash command does not exist without the
plugin, so a baseline arm would measure nothing and would double the cost of every run. This is
recorded as D7 in the plan.

Keep the existing regex graders. These assertions are about which verdict and status words appear
in the report, which `require_regex` and `forbid_regex` already handle well. No judge is needed,
and adding one would make the suite nondeterministic for no gain.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the six existing cases, when `python3 evals/run.py` runs, then all six behave exactly as before the change.
2. Given a case with a `fixture` key, when it runs, then the model's working directory is a temp copy of that fixture with its own git history, not the repository root.
3. Given a case with `single_arm` set to true, when it runs, then only the with-plugin arm executes.
4. Given `evals/README.md`, when reading it, then both keys are documented with the reason fixture cases skip the baseline arm.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `run.py` honors `fixture` and `single_arm`, both optional
- The six existing response-style cases pass unchanged
- A fixture case runs against a temp git repository, not the repository root
- `evals/README.md` documents both keys and why fixture cases are single-arm

## Out of scope

The fixture cases themselves. Those are the two eval-case beads that depend on this one.

title: Pin the verdict rules with two fixture evals
description:
## Why (Computational)

Commit `a093acc` fixed a bug where every gate skipped and the skill still reported
PASS, and a second where a configured-but-unrunnable tool degraded to SKIP instead of BLOCKED.
Both fixes live in prose, and nothing tests them, so the next edit to the Verdict Rules can
reintroduce either silently.

The stakeholder is the owner, who would then ship the regression in a release. These two rules
are the ones the skill's own text calls the reading it exists to refuse.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M6)

## Estimated size

5 files, about 130 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Two fixture repositories and two single-arm cases.

`gates-blocked-not-skip` configures a type checker in `pyproject.toml` that is absent from PATH.
It asserts the report grades that gate BLOCKED with an overall FAIL, and forbids SKIP for it.

`gates-all-skip` is a repository where every gate legitimately skips. It asserts NO GATES RAN and
forbids PASS.

The decisive step is proving each test fails when its rule is reverted by hand. A model can
produce the right verdict word by luck, so a test never observed failing is not yet a test.
Revert the missing-binary-to-BLOCKED mapping in `SKILL.md`, confirm the case fails, then restore
the line.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the `gates-blocked-not-skip` fixture, when the case runs, then the report contains BLOCKED and an overall FAIL, and does not grade that gate SKIP.
2. Given the `gates-all-skip` fixture, when the case runs, then the report contains NO GATES RAN and does not report PASS.
3. Given `SKILL.md` with the missing-binary-to-BLOCKED mapping reverted by hand, when the first case runs, then it fails; when the line is restored, it passes.
4. Given three runs of each case, when the suite finishes, then all three pass for each.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `gates-blocked-not-skip` and `gates-all-skip` exist with their fixtures
- Each passes three runs out of three with the plugin loaded
- Reverting the BLOCKED mapping in `SKILL.md` by hand makes the first case fail, and the line is
  then restored

title: Require evidence citations in the change-coverage gate
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 2 tells the model to read every test it counts and leaves no artifact proving
it did, so a plausible coverage table and a fabricated one look identical to the reader.

The stakeholder is whoever acts on a PASS from the gate the skill calls its own reason to exist.
Gate 2 is the difference between this skill and running the test command by hand, and today it
is the least verifiable thing in the report.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M3)

## Estimated size

1 file, about 45 LOC changed, band: Target.
design:
Require each counted unit test to cite the `file:line` of its key assertion, and
each end-to-end claim to quote the single line driving the real entry point (the
`subprocess.run`, the HTTP client call, the CLI runner invocation).

Quoting that line is the load-bearing part. It is what separates a real end-to-end test from an
in-process call of the handler, which the gate already forbids in its Never list but currently
has no way to detect.

Mirror the requirement in three places so it survives a partial read: Gate 2 step C, the Critical
Rules "Always" list, and the Quality Checklist. Update the Output Format worked example so the
shape is visible, not just described.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given `SKILL.md` after the change, when grepping for "Cite", then three hits appear: step C, the Always rule, and the checklist item.
2. Given the Output Format example, when reading the Change Coverage table, then at least one unit cell carries a `file:line` and one end-to-end cell carries a quoted line.
3. Given the repository, when `rumdl fmt --check .` runs, then it exits 0.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Gate 2 step C states the citation requirement for both test levels
- The Output Format example shows a `file:line` unit cell and a quoted entry-point end-to-end cell
- Critical Rules "Always" carries the rule, and the Quality Checklist carries a matching checkbox

title: Write the verdict as a JSON artifact
description:
## Why (Computational)

The report is markdown only, so no tool can read the verdict and nothing downstream
can act on it. The immediate stakeholder is the pre-push hook, which cannot gate on a conclusion
it cannot parse.

This bead also repairs a contradiction it would otherwise create. The skill states twice that it
edits nothing (`SKILL.md:356` and the checklist item at `SKILL.md:387`), and writing an artifact
makes both statements false. A skill that violates its own Critical Rules on every run is worse
than no artifact.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M4)

## Estimated size

3 files, about 80 LOC changed, band: Target.
design:
After emitting the markdown report, write `.git/quality-gates-report.json`
carrying `version`, `head`, `dirty`, `timestamp`, `scope`, `gate_source`, `verdict`, and a
per-gate array of name, status, command, and detail. Skip the write with a noted reason when the
tree is not a git repository.

Inside `.git/` on purpose: per-clone, never committed, no `.gitignore` entry needed, and it
survives until the push it is meant to inform.

The `dirty` field is recorded for a human reader and deliberately has no automated consumer. The
skill runs before the commit almost every time, so nearly every honest report is dirty, and a
hook gating on it would block constantly.

`verdict` carries one of the four Verdict Rules outcomes verbatim: PASS, FAIL, INCOMPLETE, or
NO GATES RAN.

Then narrow the two report-only rules from "writes nothing" to "writes nothing in the working
tree", and move every copy of that claim together. `commands/quality-gates.md` line 22 states it
a third time, and `skills/verify-acceptance/SKILL.md` may restate it. A surviving absolute
version is worse than none, because the next reader trusts the weaker one.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a run of the skill in a git repository, when it finishes, then `.git/quality-gates-report.json` exists and its `verdict` is one of PASS, FAIL, INCOMPLETE, NO GATES RAN.
2. Given the same run, when reading the JSON, then every gate in the markdown table appears in the `gates` array with the same status.
3. Given a run outside a git repository, when it finishes, then no artifact is written and the report states why.
4. Given the three files that state the report-only rule, when grepping for "edit" and "No file", then every hit carries the working-tree qualifier.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Step 5 writes the artifact, and skips it with a noted reason outside a git repository
- The schema carries version, head, dirty, timestamp, scope, gate_source, verdict, and gates
- `verdict` is one of the four Verdict Rules outcomes verbatim
- `SKILL.md:356` and `SKILL.md:387` carry the working-tree qualifier
- No absolute "edits nothing" claim survives in `commands/quality-gates.md` or `verify-acceptance`

## Out of scope

Reading the artifact. The pre-push consumer is the "Gate the push on a recorded FAIL verdict"
bead, which depends on this one.

title: Add a pre-push hook that runs the repository's checks
description:
## Why (Computational)

`AGENTS.md` lists nine commands under "Commands for This Repo", and running them is a
convention, not a mechanism. The only hard gate in this repository is
`.githooks/reference-transaction`, which fires on `v*` tags alone, so commits and pushes ride
entirely on the session remembering.

The stakeholder is the author who pushes a broken formatter or a failing suite and finds out
late, or never.

Author direction, recorded as D4 in the plan: enforcement is a local git hook, not GitHub
Actions. `.github/workflows/lint.yml` keeps the checks it runs today and gains nothing new.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M2)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 130 LOC, band: Target.
design:
One POSIX sh `.githooks/pre-push`, modeled on the existing
`reference-transaction` hook, running the `AGENTS.md` command list minus `evals/run.py`.

Three deliberate behaviors carry the design:

1. Run every check even after one fails, then report all failures together. A hook that stops at
   the first failure makes the author push, fail, fix, push, fail again.
2. A missing tool warns and allows, naming the tool. This follows the precedent
   `reference-transaction` set for a missing `claude`: an unpushable clone is worse than an
   unchecked push, and `rumdl` and `node` are not universally installed.
3. `TADW_PREPUSH=off` is a documented escape rather than an undocumented workaround, documented
   the way `TADW_STYLE_CORE=off` already is.

`evals/run.py` is excluded because each case is a real model call, far too slow and too expensive
to sit on a push.

A push that only deletes refs has nothing to check, so allow it. Keep output quiet on success:
one summary line, not ten.

`AGENTS.md` has a "Release gate (one-time setup per clone)" section documenting
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. Broaden it to cover both hooks rather than adding a second
setup section, since one `core.hooksPath` call now serves both.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a throwaway clone with `core.hooksPath` set and a badly formatted markdown file, when `git push --dry-run` runs, then the push is refused and the output names that file.
2. Given `TADW_PREPUSH=off` in the environment, when the same push runs, then it proceeds.
3. Given `rumdl` absent from PATH, when the push runs, then it proceeds and the output names `rumdl` as skipped.
4. Given two failing checks, when the push runs, then both failures appear in the output.
5. Given the diff against the base, when inspecting `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, then it is unchanged.
6. Given a push that only deletes a remote ref, when the hook runs, then it allows the push without running the suites.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `.githooks/pre-push` exists, is executable, and is POSIX sh
- Breaking one file's formatting makes a push fail and names that file
- `TADW_PREPUSH=off` lets the same push through
- A missing tool warns by name and allows
- Two simultaneous failures both appear; the hook does not stop at the first
- `AGENTS.md` documents both hooks under one setup section
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml` is unchanged
- The hook's wall time is measured and stated in the `AGENTS.md` section

## Out of scope

The verdict-gating stage. That is the "Gate the push on a recorded FAIL verdict" bead, which
appends a second stage to this same file.

title: Gate the push on a recorded FAIL verdict
description:
## Why (Computational)

A session can run the gates, get a FAIL, and push anyway, leaving no trace and
hitting no barrier. "Landing the Plane" in `AGENTS.md` tells the session to run the gates before
pushing, but nothing checks that it did, or what it found.

The stakeholder is the author's future self, and anyone who pulls a commit that its own QA said
was not fit to ship.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M4)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 70 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Append a second stage to the `.githooks/pre-push` file the suite-running bead
created. Git calls exactly one `pre-push` hook, so two responsibilities on the same event must
share a file with separate stages.

Read `.git/quality-gates-report.json` through `python3 -c`; do not parse JSON in sh.

The forgiveness rules are the design, not an afterthought:

- No report, or an unreadable report, warns and allows. Absence is not evidence of a problem, and
  blocking there would make the hook unusable for documentation pushes and teach people to
  disable it.
- Only a recorded verdict of FAIL blocks. The message names the verdict, the recorded head, and
  the timestamp, plus both exits: re-run `/quality-gates`, or set `TADW_PREPUSH=off`.
- A verdict whose recorded head is not an ancestor of the pushed commit warns as stale, using
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, but still allows.

Then add one line to `AGENTS.md` "Landing the Plane" step 4 noting the refusal.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a `.git/quality-gates-report.json` with verdict FAIL, when `git push --dry-run` runs in a throwaway clone, then the push is refused and the output names the verdict, the head, and the timestamp.
2. Given no report file, when the push runs, then it proceeds and prints exactly one warning line.
3. Given a report whose recorded head is not an ancestor of the pushed commit, when the push runs, then it proceeds and prints a staleness warning.
4. Given a report with verdict PASS whose head is current, when the push runs, then it proceeds silently.
5. Given the repository, when `node hooks/test-hooks.js` runs, then it passes.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- A hand-written FAIL report refuses a dry-run push in a throwaway clone
- `TADW_PREPUSH=off` lets that push through
- No report file means one warning line and a successful push
- Both stages live in one `.githooks/pre-push` and report separately
- `AGENTS.md` "Landing the Plane" step 4 notes the refusal
- `node hooks/test-hooks.js` still passes

title: Make the prompt-assets shape checkable
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 2's shape table asks the model to confirm a prompt asset "parses, is registered
where the project says, and its embedded commands are valid" without naming a single command, so
the grade is pure judgment.

This repository is the primary consumer of that row, since nearly every change here is a prompt
asset. The stakeholder is anyone whose skill shipped undiscoverable, which is what happened in
2.4.1: a `bead-audit` frontmatter scalar containing "verdicts: content" ended early, the
frontmatter failed to parse, and both name and description were dropped at load time.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M5)

## Estimated size

1 file, about 55 LOC changed, band: Target.
design:
Replace the vague cell with five items, each naming a command or a grep:

1. `claude plugin validate .` passes, so the frontmatter parses.
2. The component is registered in both places `AGENTS.md` "Common Tasks" names: the name list in
   `AGENTS.md` and the description table in `README.md`.
3. Some agent or command references the skill, or it is a documented accepted orphan (the
   `business-ideas` and `idea-wizard` precedent).
4. Every command embedded in the asset is valid: scripts it names exist at the stated paths, and
   flags it shows match the script's argparse.
5. Where the repository has an eval harness, a change to behavior-bearing prose carries an eval
   case, and its absence is a WARN naming the harness.

A table cell cannot hold a checklist, so the row points at a short subsection below the table.

State in that subsection that a script is not a component, so item 2 is N/A for one. Without that
line the next reader reports a false gap on every script this plan adds.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the subsection, when reading each of the five items, then each names a command or grep a second person could run without asking the author.
2. Given a new script with no component registration, when the checklist is applied, then item 2 is N/A by a stated rule rather than a failure.
3. Given the repository, when `rumdl fmt --check .` runs, then it exits 0.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- The prompt-assets row points at a subsection carrying all five items
- Each item names a runnable command or grep, written beside the item rather than implied
- The subsection states that a script is not a component, so item 2 is N/A for one

title: Release 2.6.0
description:
## Why (Computational)

Everything else in this plan is inert for anyone consuming the plugin from the
marketplace rather than from `main`.

The stakeholder is the plugin's users, who get none of the hardening until a version is tagged
and published.

No `auto-ok` label on purpose: tagging and pushing a release is outward-facing and should not be
settled by an agent alone.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M7)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 70 LOC, band: Target.
design:
Bump `version` in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` from 2.5.2 to 2.6.0. Minor rather
than patch, because the change adds three scripts, a git hook, a report artifact, and eval
machinery, all backward compatible with existing invocations.

Write a Keep a Changelog `## [2.6.0]` section above `## [2.5.2]`, moving anything under
`## [Unreleased]` into it. Match the existing entries' voice: each bullet leads with a bolded
sentence saying what changed and why it mattered, not a bare feature name.

Update both link-reference lines at the foot of `CHANGELOG.md`: point `[Unreleased]` at
`v2.6.0...HEAD`, and add a `[2.6.0]` line comparing `v2.5.2...v2.6.0`.

Tag last, so `.githooks/reference-transaction` validates the manifest before anything is
published. If the hook refuses, fix what `claude plugin validate` reports; never bypass with
`--no-verify`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, when reading `version`, then it is 2.6.0.
2. Given `CHANGELOG.md`, when reading the 2.6.0 section, then every script, hook, artifact, and eval addition from this plan appears.
3. Given the repository, when `git tag v2.6.0` runs, then it succeeds without `--no-verify`.
4. Given the tag pushed, when `git status` runs, then it reports up to date with origin.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` reads 2.6.0
- `CHANGELOG.md` has a 2.6.0 section covering every user-visible change, an empty Unreleased, and
  both link-reference lines updated
- `git tag v2.6.0` succeeds, meaning the release gate accepted it
- `git push --follow-tags` leaves `git status` reporting up to date with origin

## Out of scope

Any code change. This bead ships what the other beads built; if it uncovers a defect, that is a
new bead, not a fix folded in here.

title: Script the changed-set resolution
description:
## Why (Computational)

Step 2's changed-set is two git commands plus a base-resolution fallback that the
model retypes on every run, and getting it wrong silently narrows every gate.

The prose warns about one specific trap: `git diff "$BASE"...HEAD` stops at the last commit, and
this skill runs before a commit more often than after one, so the very work being checked drops
out of scope.

The stakeholder is anyone reading a scoped report that quietly covered nothing.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M1)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 230 LOC, band: Target.
design:
A stdlib Python script resolving the base by merge-base against `origin/HEAD`,
falling back to `origin/main`, then printing the union of `git diff --name-only "$BASE"` and
`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, one path per line.

The key decision is a distinct exit 3 for an unresolvable base, so the skill can tell "no remote,
fall back to --all" apart from "empty diff". The current prose conflates those two, and treating
one as the other narrows every gate to nothing while reporting confidently.

The resolved base SHA goes to stderr so stdout stays a clean path list a caller can pipe without
filtering.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a repository with a committed change, a staged change, an unstaged change, and an untracked file, when the script runs, then all four paths appear on stdout.
2. Given a repository with no remote, when the script runs, then it exits 3.
3. Given any successful run, when stdout is captured alone, then it contains no SHA and every line is a path.
4. Given a file listed in `.gitignore`, when the script runs, then that file does not appear in the output.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `changed_set.py` runs with bare `python3` and prints one path per line on stdout
- The resolved base SHA appears on stderr, never on stdout
- An unresolvable base exits 3, distinct from both success and error
- The suite covers committed, staged, unstaged, and untracked changes all appearing, plus a
  repository with no remote

## Out of scope

Wiring the script into `SKILL.md` Step 2. That belongs to the "Point the skill at the three gate
scripts" bead.

title: Script the hygiene marker count
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 7 is a one-line shell recipe carrying a subtle trap: `grep -c` exits 1 when it
counts zero, which is the clean result, so the `|| true` is load-bearing and easy to drop when a
model retypes it.

The stakeholder is the reader of a report where a clean hygiene gate was recorded as BLOCKED,
which reads as a broken toolchain rather than as good news.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M1)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 200 LOC, band: Target.
design:
A stdlib Python script taking `--base`, counting `TODO`, `FIXME`, `HACK`, and
`XXX` on added diff lines only.

The one real decision is excluding the `+++` header line. It starts with `+` and carries a path
that can itself contain a marker word, so a naive `^+` match counts a file named `TODO.md` as a
marker. That is the false positive the current shell recipe would produce.

Exit 0 at zero (the skill maps this to PASS), 1 above zero (WARN), 2 operator error (BLOCKED).
The zero-count case must exit 0 rather than any non-zero code, which is the whole reason the
current recipe needs its `|| true`.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a diff adding two lines containing TODO and FIXME, when the script runs, then it exits 1 and reports 2.
2. Given a diff whose only marker sits in a `+++ b/TODO.md` header line, when the script runs, then it exits 0 and reports 0.
3. Given a diff that deletes a TODO line and adds none, when the script runs, then it exits 0 and reports 0.
4. Given a clean diff, when the script runs, then it exits 0 and reports 0.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `check_hygiene.py` runs with bare `python3` and accepts `--base`
- The suite covers a diff adding two markers, a diff removing one, a `+++ b/TODO.md` header, and
  a clean diff
- A zero count exits 0, never a code the skill would read as BLOCKED

## Out of scope

Wiring the script into `SKILL.md` Gate 7. That belongs to the "Point the skill at the three gate
scripts" bead.

title: Script the secrets gate
description:
## Why (Computational)

Gate 6 lives as prose regexes and exclusion lists in `SKILL.md`, so the model
reassembles the pattern set, the exclusions, and the untracked-file scan on every run, and two
runs can disagree. The doc-freshness gate already proved this fails: its prose version reported
194 false positives on first contact with a real repository.

The stakeholder is anyone trusting a PASS from the secrets gate, since a quietly narrowed
pattern list reports clean while a key sits in the tree.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M1)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 330 LOC, band: Stretch.

Stretch is justified because the script and its pinned suite are one unit. Shipping the script
without the suite would land unverified detection logic, which is the exact failure this bead
exists to prevent.
design:
Port the Gate 6 rules verbatim into a stdlib-only Python script mirroring
`check_doc_paths.py` conventions: argparse, exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 operator error, and a
module docstring stating why the script exists.

Two checks. Secret-file names across both `git ls-files` and `git ls-files --others
--exclude-standard`, covering `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.p12`, `id_rsa`, `*.keystore`,
`*credential*`, and excluding `.env.example`, `.env.sample`, `.env.template`. Then prefixed key
formats in content only: `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`, `ghp_`, `xox[baprs]-`, `sk-ant-`, and
`-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----`. Generic long hex or base64 matching is deliberately absent;
it fires on lockfile hashes and minified assets, and a gate that cries wolf gets ignored.

The load-bearing design constraint is that the matched value never reaches output, only
`file:line` and the pattern name, so the report cannot copy the secret into one more place.

A comment block at the top of the test file maps each prose rule to the test pinning it. That
mapping is what proves the port neither narrowed nor widened detection.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a temp repository with an untracked, unignored `.env`, when the script runs, then it exits 1 and names that file.
2. Given the same fake `AKIA` key in `src/` and in `node_modules/`, when the script runs, then only the `src/` hit is reported.
3. Given any finding, when the report prints, then it contains `file:line` and the pattern name, and does not contain the matched value.
4. Given this repository as the working tree, when the script runs, then it exits 0.
5. Given the test suite, when it runs with bare `python3`, then every test passes and no third-party module is imported.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- `check_secrets.py` runs with bare `python3` and imports nothing outside the standard library
- Running it against this repository exits 0
- The suite covers a tracked `.env`, an untracked-but-unignored `.env`, an excluded
  `.env.example`, a fake `AKIA` key in source, the same key under `node_modules/`, and a clean tree
- A test asserts the planted key's value reaches neither stdout nor stderr
- A comment block maps every Gate 6 pattern and exclusion to its test

## Out of scope

Wiring the script into `SKILL.md`. That is the "Point the skill at the three gate scripts" bead,
which depends on this one.

title: Point the skill at the three gate scripts
description:
## Why (Computational)

The three gate scripts are inert until `SKILL.md` invokes them. Until then the model
still hand-rolls the checks, and the scripts are dead code carrying a false sense of coverage.

A second stakeholder is the next reader of `AGENTS.md`, whose "Commands for This Repo" block is
the discovery surface for every check in this repository. A suite absent from that block is a
suite nobody runs.

Plan: docs/plans/quality-gates-hardening.md (M1)

## Estimated size

2 files, about 70 LOC changed, band: Target.
design:
Rewrite Gates 6 and 7 and Step 2 to invoke the bundled scripts with an
exit-status mapping table, following the pattern Gate 5 already set for `check_doc_paths.py`.

Keep the rationale prose in place. The script encodes the rules; the prose still explains why
they are what they are, which is what stops a later editor from "simplifying" the exclusion list
back into a false-positive machine. Specifically preserve: why prefixed key formats only, why an
untracked `.env` matters, and why `git diff "$BASE"...HEAD` is the wrong basis.

Keep Gate 6's stated preference for a project-configured scanner. The bundled script is the
fallback, not a replacement for `gitleaks` where a project already runs it.

Then register the three new suites in the `AGENTS.md` "Commands for This Repo" block.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given `SKILL.md` after the change, when reading Gates 6, 7 and Step 2, then each carries a `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/..."` invocation and no inline pattern list.
2. Given `AGENTS.md`, when reading "Commands for This Repo", then all three new `test_*.py` paths appear and each resolves on disk.
3. Given the repository, when `python3 skills/quality-gates/scripts/check_doc_paths.py --repo-root .` runs, then it exits 0, proving the newly documented paths are real.
4. Given the repository, when `rumdl fmt --check .` runs, then it exits 0.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)

- Gates 6 and 7 and Step 2 each invoke their script and carry an exit-status mapping table
- The inline regex lists and shell recipes are gone from those sections
- The rationale paragraphs survive: why prefixed formats only, why an untracked `.env` matters,
  why `...HEAD` is the wrong basis
- Gate 6 still prefers a project-configured scanner over the bundled script
- `AGENTS.md` lists all three new suites

title: Diagnose why the sentence limit fails in self-reports
description:
## Why (Computational)

The twenty-five-word sentence limit is the least enforced rule in house-response-style, and it
fails in the one place an agent writes most often: reporting its own work.

Measured 2026-08-05 on evals/cases/self-report-plainly at five runs, sonnet, with-plugin arm:
four of five runs broke the grader's 35-word ceiling, at 44, 48, 54, and 64 words. The skill's
own limit is 25. The label check passed 5 of 5 in the same runs, so this is not a wording
problem in the label rule.

This was invisible until PR #20. The flat label ban failed every run first, so the runner never
reported the sentence failures underneath it. Removing one failure exposed another.

The stakeholder is the reader of every agent report, who gets a 64-word sentence carrying four
joined claims where the rule promises two short ones.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out main with the plugin loaded.
2. Run `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY python3 evals/run.py --case self-report-plainly --runs 5 --model sonnet`.
3. Read the `max_sentence_words` result for each of the five runs in the with-plugin arm.

**Expected behavior:** every sentence in the self-report sits at or under the 25-word limit the
skill states, and therefore comfortably under the grader's looser 35-word ceiling recorded at
`evals/cases/self-report-plainly/case.json:5`.

**Actual behavior:** four of five runs exceed 35 words, at 44, 48, 54, and 64. The label check
passes 5 of 5 in the same runs, so the failure is specific to sentence length.

**Environment / version:** sonnet, with-plugin arm, measured 2026-08-05 on main as of PR #20.
design:
Three hypotheses, to be tested one at a time, each with a five-run measurement:

H1. The prompt invites it. The case asks for 'one short paragraph of plain prose', and a model
reads 'paragraph' as one narrative unit, then joins clauses to fill it. Test by adding a second
prompt that asks for a report with no shape constraint, and comparing sentence lengths.

H2. The rule is too far from its use. The split-word list ('which', 'so', 'but', 'since',
'because') lives in STE rule 6. The 'Report your own work plainly' section does not reference
it, so the model applies the contract without applying the limit. Test by adding one sentence
to that section pointing at the cut list.

H3. The limit is unreachable for this content. A self-report carries four facts (count,
failure, action, reason), and four facts may not fit two sentences under 25 words each. Test by
writing the target answer by hand and counting.

Change one thing per measurement. Do not lower the 35-word grader ceiling: it is already looser
than the 25-word rule, and loosening it again would stop it measuring anything.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the three hypotheses, when each is tested at five runs, then the result of each is written into the bead or into evals/README.md, naming which one held.
2. Given the chosen fix, when evals/cases/self-report-plainly runs at five runs, then max_sentence_words passes at least 4 of 5.
3. Given the same five runs, then the label check and all four substance checks still pass 5 of 5, so the fix did not trade one rule for another.
4. Given the fix, when evals/run.py is inspected, then the max_sentence_words ceiling is still 35 and the skill's stated limit is still 25.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- The diagnosis names which hypothesis held, with the run counts behind it.
- self-report-plainly passes max_sentence_words at least 4 of 5 without any grader loosening.
- The label and substance checks are unchanged at 5 of 5.

## Scope boundary
Changing the 25-word rule itself is OUT of scope. If the measurement shows 25 is unreachable
for a four-fact report, that is a finding and a follow-up bead, not an edit made under this one.

## Estimated size
1 to 3 files (the `house-response-style` section, possibly one new eval case), ~40 LOC, plus
15 to 25 model runs. Band: Target (provisional - the LOC is inferred from the How, author to
confirm; the run count is effort, not diff, and does not enter the band).

title: Author style-testing core, reconcile style-rspec, and wire it for dispatch (Part 1)
description:
## Why (Computational)

This workbench has no framework-independent test-writing guidance. Its only test skill,
style-rspec (496 lines), is RSpec-on-Rails specific, and a grep across skills/ and hooks/ finds
zero guidance for pytest, Vitest, Jest, XCTest, Swift Testing, or Minitest. The owner works in
multiple languages and no longer uses RSpec, so the repo's richest style asset is unusable to them.

The universal core every other style skill sits on (hooks/style-core.md, 72 lines) is a
production-code core: its nine principles cover abstraction, unit size, interfaces, dependency
injection, tell-don't-ask, composition, errors, the step-down rule, and naming. None address test
structure. So the gap is not "style-rspec lacks a core" (it already points at style-core.md at
lines 27-29); it is that no testing core exists for anything to sit on.

Reaching the skill matters as much as writing it. agents/software-engineer.md:35-39 and
agents/code-reviewer.md:38-40 dispatch to style skills by file extension, and test files have no
routing entry anywhere. A skill wired only into AGENTS.md and README.md would ship unreachable,
which is exactly the state style-rspec is in today: well written, documented, never loaded.

Plan: docs/plans/feature-plan-style-testing.md

## Estimated size
10 files, net about -57 LOC (+235 new core, -400 rspec trim, +108 wiring and gates). Band: Target.
design:
Mirror the established delta structure. Author skills/style-testing/SKILL.md as a genuine testing
core of 14 principles (10 transposed from style-rspec, 4 net-new: determinism, behavior-not-
implementation naming, what not to test, precise assertions), then rewrite style-rspec to carry
only RSpec deltas, opening with a pointer to style-testing the way style-python:26 points at
hooks/style-core.md.

Key decisions:

D2. The principles body names no framework; exactly one fenced appendix maps each principle to its
pytest, Vitest/Jest, XCTest/Swift Testing, and Minitest idiom. Without the appendix the skill is
platitudes; with it inside the principles it stops being a core. Enforced by a static check
script, not by author discipline.

D3. Keep style-rspec as a roughly 90-line delta rather than deleting it. Cheap, keeps
review-rails:30 resolving, and deletion is irreversible.

D4. No sibling delta skills (style-pytest, style-vitest). Wait for duplication before abstracting.

D6. The frontmatter description is a first-class deliverable with its own invocation test.
style-rspec's description ("RSpec tests in Rails apps") is scoped so narrowly it can never fire on
the owner's current work; that failure mode must not be reproduced.

D7. The cheap deterministic gates (static leak check, invocation test) ship here. The expensive
behavioral A/B eval ships in Part 2, so Part 1 can prove the skill is correct-by-construction,
wired, and reachable, but not that it is useful. That limitation is accepted and named.

Milestones: M1 author core; M2 rspec delta (own commit, pre-rewrite SHA captured first); M3 doc
rewire (review-rails:30, AGENTS.md:168 and :362, README.md:135); M3b dispatch rewire
(software-engineer.md:35-39 and :54, code-reviewer.md:38-40, python-feature-dev.md:13) adding test
file patterns; M5a static and invocation gates.

Supersedes this bead's original design, which assumed the owner still used RSpec and required
registering the skill in .claude-plugin/plugin.json. That file registers zero components; the
claim traces to a documentation defect in AGENTS.md, tracked separately in Part 2.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given a reader opens skills/style-testing/SKILL.md, when they read the principles, anti-patterns, escape hatches, and checklist sections, then no rule names a construct from any specific test framework (definition; criterion 2 is its enforcement).
2. Given `python3 skills/style-testing/scripts/check_framework_leak.py`, when run, then it exits 0 and reports zero leaked framework tokens outside the appendix and the frontmatter.
3. Given a reader opens skills/style-rspec/SKILL.md, when they read its opening section, then it names style-testing as the core it extends, and the file is under 120 lines.
4. Given `grep -rn "style-testing" AGENTS.md README.md skills/review-rails/SKILL.md`, when run, then all three files match.
5. Given skills/review-rails/SKILL.md previously deferred test style to style-rspec, when the rewire lands, then it defers to style-testing first and names style-rspec only as the RSpec-conditional delta, and both skills still exist on disk.
6. Given the orphan check in /validate-plugin, whose rule is "skills not referenced by any agent or command", when run, then style-testing is referenced by at least one file in agents/ and is not flagged as an orphan.
7. Given the M5a invocation test, when run over its 8 test-writing prompts and 3 non-test controls, then at least 7 test prompts invoke style-testing and at most 1 control false-fires.
8. Given `git log --oneline -- skills/style-rspec/SKILL.md`, when inspected after M2, then the rewrite is an isolated commit revertible without touching M1 or M3.
notes:
## Done when (Acceptance)
- skills/style-testing/SKILL.md exists with 14 framework-free principles plus the fenced framework-idiom appendix.
- Its frontmatter description names the activity and the frameworks, so the skill can actually be invoked.
- style-rspec retains no guidance that would read as correct advice with the RSpec nouns stripped out, and is under 120 lines.
- style-testing is referenced by at least one file in agents/, so /validate-plugin does not flag it as an orphan.
- Test file patterns route to style-testing in software-engineer, code-reviewer, and python-feature-dev.
- check_framework_leak.py exits 0, and the invocation test clears 7 of 8.

## Scope boundary
Efficacy (does the skill measurably improve the tests a model writes) is deliberately NOT proven
here. That is Part 2. Part 1 ships a skill that is correct-by-construction, wired, and reachable.

## Progress (in_progress)
Done and verified: M1 (skills/style-testing/SKILL.md, 269 lines, 14 principles + fenced appendix),
M2 (style-rspec 496 -> 119 lines; baseline SHA f82c91e29a2fd395de2c77f4ab4ad5d2d4729bae; isolated
commit), M3 (AGENTS.md, README.md, review-rails), M3b (software-engineer, code-reviewer,
python-feature-dev), M5a static half (check_framework_leak.py, verified against a planted-leak
control).

Passing: AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC8.

## BLOCKED: AC7 needs a fresh session
The invocation battery cannot run in the session that created the skill. Claude Code loads its
skill registry at session start, so style-testing is absent from every subagent's available-skills
list until a restart. A probe subagent confirmed it: style_testing_present = false.

Running the battery now would score 0/8 for a reason unrelated to description quality, which is
what AC7 is meant to measure. Run it first thing in a new session, before any other work.
close_reason: Part 1 complete: all 8 acceptance criteria pass, including AC7 at 8/8 positive and 0/3 control
